subject: Next steps: CloudWave comparative QA + model-quality test plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cloudwave.com>, Amit Shah <amit@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: CloudWave comparative QA & next evals

Hi Priya / Amit,

Thanks for the time today — good first sync. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: we heard three priorities from you on the demo/call:

- Quality parity vs hyperscalers on domain docs (finance/legal templates) — focused on hallucination/factuality
- Tail latency targets for interactive workflows (p95/p99) — goal: p95 < 300ms for 512-token inference in your staging region
- Cost profile / per-request delta compared to your current managed endpoints

Immediate asks from our side (what we'll run if you confirm):

1) Comparative QA run: Redwood-hosted model variant vs your two hyperscaler baselines (we'll use the public endpoints you listed). We'll run the benchmark prompts you shared plus a closed-book set from your internal snippets.
2) Hallucination/regression checks: focused prompt set that stresses dates, named entities, and instruction-following (see attached PROMPTSET-783).
3) Latency sweep: end-to-end measurements with a 95th/99th tail analysis and KV-cache on/off.

Proposed owners & ETA:
- Redwood lead: Marcus Lin (technical test plan + scripts) — deliver baseline artifacts by 2026-12-01 EOD
- Redwood contact (sales/coord): me (Rachel) — schedule a follow-up to review results 2026-12-02 or 12-03
- CloudWave: please confirm dataset link(s) and whether the staging endpoints are reachable from us (IP allowlist or shared test account).

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Hallucination rate on closed-book factual prompts <= 1.0% (we'll compute F1/precision on extracted entities)
- Instruction-following pass rate >= 95% on the rubric items
- p95 latency <= 300ms for 512 tokens (measured across 30k requests with continuous batching enabled)

I've attached: promptset-cloudwave-v1.json (sample prompts), inference-delta-sample.csv (example diff rows), rdw-hyperscaler-baseline-notes.pdf (initial kernel/quantization notes).

Please confirm you want us to proceed with the comparative runs and share the dataset link or a staging API key for the hyperscaler endpoints. If you prefer, we can run against the public endpoints you already provided — just say so.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

- Priority A is hallucination on our legal templates and customer-facing summaries (we'll provide ~120 prompts drawn from redacted templates).
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms is ideal; p99 under 700ms is also useful for us to understand.
- For hyperscaler baselines, use the public endpoints for GCP/GenericCloud (we'll try to get staging keys but no blocker).

Dataset link: https://cloudwave.sharepoint.com/sites/eng-evals/CloudWavePromptBundle.zip (password: RedactedInEmail)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 2:02 PM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum...

Thanks — outlining the test plan and specific artifacts I'll deliver. High-level approach: run parallel offline runs against each endpoint (Redwood variant vs hyperscaler public endpoints) and then a small-scale end-to-end latency sweep from our US-west test runners.

Test components:
- Prompt sets: PROMPTSET-783 (closed-book factual checks, NER extraction), PROMPTSET-784 (instruction-following), PROMPTSET-785 (hallucination stressors).
- Metrics: hallucination_rate (entity hallucinations / total checks), exact_match for closed facts, instruction_pass_rate (rubric), latency_p50/p95/p99, token_cost_estimate (per 1k tokens).
- Baselines: GCP-API-v2, HyperscaleX-infer, Redwood-llama-quant (v1.4) pinned. We'll document model sizes and quantization kernels in notes.
- Scripts: run_eval.sh + compare_delta.py (produces inference-delta-sample.csv). I'll upload container + results to the Drive folder.

Proposed numeric thresholds for the first pass (we can refine after initial run):
- hallucination_rate <= 1.0% on closed-book set
- instruction_pass_rate >= 95%
- latency p95 <= 300ms (512 tokens, KV-cache enabled)

Schedule & deliverables:
- 2026-12-01 17:00 PST: initial batch-run artifacts (raw outputs + inference-delta CSV)
- 2026-12-02 10:00 PST: short readout (1 page) + folder with comparisons
- 2026-12-03: joint review call (if you want deeper dive)

Notes/requests for CloudWave: please confirm the SharePoint bundle link works for our test runners (we need the unzipped JSON lines file and a small reference index to run closed-book retrieval tests). Also, if you have any no-go tokens or PII redaction rules for the redacted prompts, include that in the shared docs.

I'll attach the initial run script and a short checklist.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
